messages:
Priya: Heads-up — nightly perf regression after merging runtime/selector:small-fallback. P50 up ~15% on a couple of workloads. Attached two nsys captures (before/after).
Connor: Can you paste the nsys links/artifacts? quick diff would help.
Priya: perf-bot posted them: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/bs/1769456600/before.nsys and https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/bs/1769456700/after.nsys
Priya: Quick summary from spot-check: before matmul_v2 total 112ms, after 168ms. memcpy kernels also show up a lot more in the after trace.
Yuko: interesting. Any change to KV cache lifecycle or batching that might increase memcpy churn?
Priya: The selector change forces fallback to the 'compat' kernel for some seq-len buckets; that kernel does an explicit staging buffer copy path we thought cheap. Looks like it's not.
Connor: ok please run flops/occupancy and cudaMemcpy counts. NVTX markers around the staging path would help isolate.
Priya: ran quick cupti summary: before: memcopy count 42, total 8.1ms; after: memcopy count 128, total 39.5ms. Occupancy for matmul_v2 dropped from 0.98 -> 0.65 when compat kernel used.
Priya: snippet from nsys CLI export: 
```
KERNEL: matmul_v2 | calls: 56 | avg 2.0ms | total 112.0ms
KERNEL: matmul_v2 (compat) | calls: 56 | avg 3.0ms | total 168.0ms
KERNEL: memcpy_h2d | calls: 128 | total 39.5ms
```
Connor: That suggests the compat kernel is lower occupancy + extra host staging. Could be introduced by the kernel selector threshold math or an ABI change in the kernel build.
Yuko: Could also be that the compat kernel is getting selected for batch sizes that used to hit the optimized path because of a float rounding change in the selector.
Priya: I'm going to run a focused perfetto/nvprof that captures CPU-side scheduling and string together the nvtx ranges so we can see how batching aligns with memcpy spikes. Will post shortly.
perf-bot: CI perf job completed. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/bs/1769456900/perf-summary.html (contains perf counters / nvprof reports) :white_check_mark:
Connor: Nice. Priya, want to bisect between commit sha a1b2c3d (last-good) and d4e5f6g (first-bad)? I can provide a bisect script that runs a small reproducible microbenchmark and collects minimal nsys snapshots.
Priya: yes please. I started a local bisect smoke: `git bisect start d4e5f6g a1b2c3d` then `git bisect run ./tools/perf/bisect-runner.sh` — runner returns non-zero when p50 exceeds threshold.
Connor: Perfect. Make sure runner also dumps NVTX markers and uploads to perf-bot. Example runner snippet: 
```
python perf/bench_infer.py --iters 50 --batch 8 --nvtx --outfile trace.nsys
upload-artifact trace.nsys
```
Priya: Doing that now. First few commits show selector code touching the float->int bucket rounding in kernel_selector.cpp.
Yuko: If bucket rounding is the culprit, we should add unit tests for selector determinism and a microbenchmark that asserts which kernel gets chosen per (batch, seq_len).
Priya: Agreed. For immediate mitigation, we can add a guard to fallback to the optimized kernel when heuristics are within epsilon of boundary. Quick patch reduces p50 back to within 2% in local runs.
Connor: Good emergency patch. But need proper rollback for correctness: either fix rounding or adjust selector thresholds.
Priya: Action items: 1) finish git bisect + attach nsys on the exact commit that flips selector decision. 2) Add unit tests for kernel selection (deterministic across compilers) 3) Add perf microbenchmark to CI (fast) that fails on >5% regression and uploads minimal traces. 4) Revert or fix selector math depending on bisect result.
Yuko: I'll pick up the unit tests and CI microbenchmark. Connor, can you review the emergency guard?
Connor: Yep will review PR once you open it. Also will add a perf-checker entry to flag sudden memcpy count spikes.
Priya: Uploaded the first bisect artifacts: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/bisect/1769457000/ (includes trace from commit ff33aa which is the first bad)
Yuko: awesome. Thanks Priya. :rocket:
Priya: I'll keep posting updates here as bisect narrows it down. If anyone wants to reproduce locally, use the perf-bisect.sh and make sure you have cuda driver 535+ and nsys 2024.3.
Connor: Thanks — very clear.
infra-bot: Deployed temporary perf job to on-demand infra pool (tag: bisect-hotpath). Logs: https://infra.redwood/logs/1769457050
Priya: closing loop once bisect has single commit. current range down to 8 commits.
Yuko: Great. Ping when it's 1 commit and we'll triage kernel source changes.
